top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) are a mature, experimentally verified achievement distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes: the magic-wavelength idea lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once and has been confirmed independently near 10^-18 in several laboratories. The two-name allocation needs no arbitrary cut, the citation scope is clean, and the precision-measurement payoff (redshift tests, constants and dark-matter bounds) is a genuine physics result, so an award is preferable to no award.
